1. By this application under section 483(3) of the Bhartiya Nagrik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, the applicant-original complainant has prayed for the following reliefs;
"(A) Your Lordship may be pleased to cancel the bail granted to respondent No.2 vide impugned order dated 07.02.2022 passed in Criminal Misc. Application No.164 of 2022 by learned 3rd Additional Sessions Judge, Gandhinagar (at Annexure-A hereto);

(B) During the pendency and final disposal of the present application, YOUR LORDSHIPS may be pleased to cancel bail granted to respondent no.2 vide impugned order dated 07.02.20222 passed in Criminal Misc.

(C ) Pass any such other and/or further orders that may be thought just and proper, in the facts and circumstances of the present case."
2.

The sum and substance of the allegations made in the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined FIR is that the respondents-accused were running the business in the name and style as Jalaram Industries, and on 27.06.2019, they placed an order of 22 Metric Tons of Palmolein Oil with the present applicant-original complainant on telephone, upon which, immediately the original complainant supplied 21,890 metric tons of Palmolein Oil to the respondents-accused amounting to Rs.13,97,458/- along with the tax invoice,
however, upon demand being made by the original complainant to pay the bill amount, the respondents-accused, initially avoided to make the payment for one reason or the other, and when insisted by the original complainant, made payment of Rs.4,32,486/- in installment, and has not paid the remaining amount of Rs.8,64,972/- till today, and therefore, upon constant demands being made by the original complainant on phone, the respondents-accused declined to make the payment, and thereby committed an offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust.
3.

Apprehending their arrest pursuant to the registration of the aforesaid FIR, the respondent-accused preferred anticipatory bail application before the learned Principal Sessions Judge, Gandhinagar, which came to be allowed vide order dated 07.02.2022, and enlarged the respondents- accused on anticipatory bail.
4. Being aggrieved, the present applicant-original complainant is here before this Court with the present application.

5. Learned advocate Mr. Nishit P. Gandhi appearing for the NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined original complainant, submitted that the bail granted to the respondents-accused deserves to be cancelled.

He submitted that the Sessions Judge ought not to have exercised his discretion solely on the ground that there a business relationship between the complainant and the accused persons, and that there was a delay in registering the FIR, but the learned Judge also, while considering the bail application, ought to have taken into consideration the other relevant aspects of the matter, and therefore, the impugned order dated 07.02.2022 passed by the learned Sessions Judge is illegal and without giving any reasonings.
He submitted that the impugned order passed by the Sessions Judge reflects total non-application of mind.

Learned advocate Mr. Gandhi further submitted the accused persons are the headstrong persons, and are trying to create obstacle in the smooth investigation, and are threatening the witnesses of dire consequences.

He submitted that there is a prima facie case made out against the respondents-accused, and on bare perusal of the FIR, the essential ingredients to constitute the offence, as alleged, are clearly spelt out.
He also submitted that moreover considering the punishment prescribed for the alleged offences, discretion ought not to have been exercised in favour of the accused persons.

Moreover, the accused are headstrong persons, and the respondent No.2 is administering threats to the original complainant and other family members of severe Nikhilkumar Jivanbhai Kamani vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134697617/
2 consequences.

sentences.text: Hhe submitted that the impugned order of bail is almost like a judgment of acquittal ignoring relevant aspects and principles as regards grant of bail in an offence of cheating and criminal breach of trust.
Thus, it has been submitted that NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined the bail granted in favour of the respondents-accused deserves to be cancelled.
6. None remain present on behalf of the respondents- accused.

7. Heard the learned advocate appearing for the applicant and the learned APP, as also perused the record.
8.

The case on hand pertains to cancellation of bail granted to the accused, and according to me, in an application for cancellation of bail, the conduct subsequent to release on bail and the supervening circumstances are the relevant factors to be kept in mind while deciding the cancellation of bail application.

It is no doubt true that the error being committed by the learned trial judge as well as the non-consideration of relevant aspects while setting the accused at liberty are also the relevant factors to be borne in mind at the time of deciding cancellation of bail application, still the same do not have much significance, on the basis of which, the order granting bail to the accused can be reversed, as it can be taken into consideration and determined during the course of trial.

The consideration of cancellation of bail is different from the consideration for grant of bail, and the bail can be cancelled only on existence of cogent and overwhelming circumstances, but not on re-appreciation of the facts of the case.
It is a settled law that cancellation of bail should not be by way of punishment even if prima facie case against the accused is established.

9. I have also gone through the order passed by the learned NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined Sessions Judge, and it appears from the same that all the relevant aspects germane to the grant of bail have been considered by the Sessions Judge and, therefore, the discretion exercised could not be said to be perverse or illegal in any manner.
10. I have also gone through the averments made in the application.

It appears from the same that,
the cancellation is sought for on the ground that some relevant aspects were not taken into consideration by the learned trial judge while enlarging the accused on bail.

It is the case of the complainant that he was cheated by the respondents-accused, however, to establish the said charges, it seems from the impugned judgment as well as the materials placed before this Court, that the original complainant has not produced any cogent and convincing evidence, on the basis of which, the court could decline to grant anticipatory bail to the respondents-accused, as also for this Court to cancel the same.
11. Here, in the case at hand, it is not the case of the complainant that the respondents-accused has breached any of the conditions imposed upon him by the trial court while being released on bail.

The respondents-accused are at liberty since February, 2022 i.e.. for more than three years, and during this period, not a single incident of non-compliance of the order passed by the trial court is reported against the respondents-accused, or brought on record before this Court.

Hence, solely on Nikhilkumar Jivanbhai Kamani vs State Of Gujarat on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134697617/

12.

Moreover, while considering degree of burden of prove lie upon prosecution or complainant/Informant, when an application for cancellation of bail moved, is not to the extent of proving by a mathematical certainty or beyond reasonable doubt but it must establish its case by showing on a preponderance of probabilities that accused has attempted or may attempt to or tamper or has tampered with witnesses.
It may also be proved by test of balance of probabilities that accused has abused his liberty or it may show that there is reasonable apprehension that he will interfere with course of justice.
This Court approved Bombay High Court decision in Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain 60

entities.text: Madhukar Purshottam Jondkar vs. Talab Haji Hussain
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Bombay Law Reporter 465 that test adopted by the Court would be, whether material placed before it is such as to lead to the conclusion that there is a strong prima facie case that accused if allowed to be at large he would tamper with prosecution witnesses and impede course of justice.
Mere unfounded apprehension or self imagined threat by prosecution or Informant-Complainant would not justify cancellation of bail, granted to accused.

13. In Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481, the Court held that grounds for cancellation of bail under Sections 437(5) and 439(2) are identical, namely, bail granted under Section 437(1) or (2) or Section 439(1) can be cancelled where (i) accused misuses his liberty by indulging in similar criminal activity, (ii) interferes with the course of investigation, (iii) attempts to tamper with evidence or witnesses, (iv) threatens NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined witnesses or indulges in similar activities which would hamper smooth investigation, (v) there is likelihood of his fleeing to another country, (vi) attempts to make himself scarce by going underground or becoming unavailable to the investigating agency, (vii) attempts to place himself beyond the reach of his surety, etc.
14.

entities.text: Raghubir Singh vs. State of Bihar (1986) 4 SCC 481
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was also held that above grounds are illustrative and not exhaustive.
Rejection of bail stands on one footing but cancellation of bail is a harsh order since it interferes with liberty of individual and must not be lightly resorted to.

15. In Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349, the Court held that rejection of bail in a non-bailable case at initial stage and cancellation of bail so granted, has to be dealt with and considered on different basis.

entities.text: Dolat Ram and others vs. State of Haryana (1995) 1 SCC 349
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing cancellation of bail, already granted.

Court further said that generally speaking grounds of cancellation of bail, broadly i.e. illustrative and not exhaustive are : (i) interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice; (ii) evasion or attempt to evade due course of justice;

In CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296, in para 23,
Court said :
"....that there is difference between yardstick for cancellation of bail and appeal against the order granting bail.

entities.text: CBI, Hyderabad vs. Subramani Gopalakrishnan and others (2011) 5 SCC 296
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Very cogent and overwhelming circumstances are necessary for an order directing the cancellation of bail already granted.

Generally speaking, the grounds for cancellation of bail are, interference or attempt to interfere with the due course of administration of justice or evasion or attempt to evade the due course of justice or abuse of the concessions granted to the accused in any manner.
These are all only few illustrative materials.
The satisfaction of the Court on the basis of the materials placed on record of the possibility of the accused absconding is another reason justifying the cancellation of bail.

In other words, bail once granted should not be cancelled in a mechanical manner without considering whether any supervening circumstances have rendered it no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow the accused to retain his freedom by enjoying the concession of bail during the trial."

18. Position, influence and resources of accused have also been held relevant factors to adjudge whether accused is likely to interfere with administration of justice, trial or tamper with witness or evidence.

19. Considerations and relevant aspects by a Court while granting a bail are different than those when an application for cancellation of bail has come up before the Court and this aspect has been considered by a three-Judges Bench of Supreme Court in State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411 wherein the Bench had an occasion to consider an order dated 11.04.1978 passed by Delhi High NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined Court rejecting Delhi Administration's application for cancellation of bail of respondent Sanjay Gandhi.

entities.text: State (Delhi Administration) vs. Sanjay Gandhi (1978) 2 SCC 411
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The Court observed that rejection of bail, when bail applied is one thing;
cancellation of bail already granted is quite another.
It is easier to reject a bail application in a non-bailable case than to cancel a bail granted in such a case.

Cancellation of bail necessarily involves review of a decision already made and can, by and large, be permitted only, if, by reason of supervening circumstances, it would be no longer conducive to a fair trial to allow accused to retain his freedom during the trial.

entities.text: X vs. The State of Telangana and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2018)16 SCC 511, accused, a Film Producer, based in Mumbai, was charged of offences under Sections 376, 342, 493, 506, 354(C) of IPC.
Accused got anticipatory bail from Sessions Judge on 13.01.2017 and had advantage of that order for about eight months.
The said order was cancelled by Sessions Judge on the ground that accused has not disclosed that he was also accused in 2G Spectrum case.
This cancellation order was affirmed by High Court and also by Supreme Court.
Thereafter accused moved a bail application under Section 439 Cr.P.C., which was allowed by High Court and accused was released on bail.
This order was challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
Upholding the said order, Court said that bail once granted should not be cancelled unless a cogent case, based on supervening event has been made out.
21. In Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors.

entities.text: Seema Singh vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2018) 16 SCC 10 bail granted to accused by High Court in the case registered under Sections 498-A, 302, 120-B IPC was NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/4408/2022 ORDER DATED: 10/07/2025 undefined challenged in appeal before Supreme Court.
The Court noticed that accused-2's bail application was rejected by Special Judicial Magistrate, CBI, Ghaziabad and thereafter bail was granted by High Court.
The Court said that gravity of offence is a relevant factor but not the sole ground to deny bail if there are other overwhelming circumstances justifying grant of bail.
Noticing special feature, Court upheld order of High Court granting bail.

22. Thus, the broad principles, which are to be considered by this Court while granting bail and when bail is already granted but an application for cancellation has come up for consideration, as discussed above, show that there is no thumb rule in both the situations.
However, it is true that factors relevant for grant of bail are different and approach required to be adopted while considering application for cancellation of bail is different.

23. Looking to above exposition of law as also the fact and circumstances of the case, I find that there is no material available on record to show any justification for cancellation of bail after more than three years and, therefore, order of cancellation of bail cannot be justified at this stage.
24.
In the result, the present application fails and is hereby rejected.
Notice is discharged.
